scenes.visual: Title card 'A Field Is a Sum' over a cartoon grassland of square plots. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: species A = GOLD; species B = TEAL; further species = CORAL, SLATE BLUE and SAND; complementarity = GREEN bar; selection = VIOLET bar; a plot's total biomass = a DARK OUTLINE drawn around the stacked species bars; the expected (monoculture-based) yield = a DASHED grey bar. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Plants are simple cartoons; bars computed from the stated numbers are labelled 'computed'; anything else is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Sow sixteen plant species in a field instead of one. Why would that field grow more? And why would its total change less from year to year?
scenes.visual: Split screen: left, a square plot with one kind of tuft (GOLD); right, a square plot packed with sixteen differently coloured tufts. Two question marks appear: one over a 'biomass' label, one over a small wiggling line labelled 'year to year'.
scenes.narration: Sow sixteen plant species in a field instead of one. Why would that field grow more? And why would its total change less from year to year?

scenes.tts: Start with one plain fact. A plot's production is the sum of what each of its species produces. Every year, ecologists clip the plants, dry them and weigh them.
scenes.visual: The sixteen-species plot's tufts lift out and become sixteen thin coloured bars that stack into one column; a DARK OUTLINE closes around the stack, labelled 'total = sum of species'. Small icons slide past along the bottom: shears, drying oven, balance; label 'clip, dry, weigh each year'.
scenes.narration: Start with one plain fact. A plot's production is the sum of what each of its species produces. Every year, ecologists clip the plants, dry them and weigh them.

scenes.tts: Grow species A alone, shown in gold. It makes a tall pile of biomass. Grow species B alone, in teal. It makes a short pile.
scenes.visual: Two monoculture bars grow from a baseline: GOLD bar 'A alone: 400 g per square metre', TEAL bar 'B alone: 100 g per square metre'. Labels 'monoculture'. Computed.
scenes.narration: Grow species A alone, shown in gold. It makes a tall pile of biomass. Grow species B alone, in teal. It makes a short pile.

scenes.tts: Now sow them half and half. If mixing neither helped nor hurt, each species would make half of its yield alone. That gives the dashed bar, the expected yield.
scenes.visual: Half of the GOLD bar (200) and half of the TEAL bar (50) slide over and stack into a DASHED grey outline bar labelled 'expected: 250'. Label 'sown 50 : 50'. Computed.
scenes.narration: Now sow them half and half. If mixing neither helped nor hurt, each species would make half of its yield alone. That gives the dashed bar, the expected yield.

scenes.tts: But the real mixture grows taller than the dashed bar. That gap is the extra yield. With an even sowing, the benchmark is the average monoculture, not the best one. Here the mixture only matches species A grown alone.
scenes.visual: A stacked bar rises beside the dashed one: GOLD 300 under TEAL 100, total 400 in a DARK OUTLINE. A bracket between the dashed top (250) and the outline top (400) reads 'extra yield: +150'. A faint ghost of the GOLD monoculture bar (400) appears to the side, labelled 'best monoculture: 400', with a note 'benchmark = average monoculture'. Computed.
scenes.narration: But the real mixture grows taller than the dashed bar. That gap is the extra yield. With an even sowing, the benchmark is the average monoculture, not the best one. Here the mixture only matches species A grown alone.

scenes.tts: Where could the extra come from? Perhaps the species use soil and light differently, or help each other. That is complementarity. Or a richer draw is more likely to include a species that yields highly alone. If such high-yielding species also gain the most relative to their yield alone, that is selection. Both can act at once.
scenes.visual: Over the bracket, two labels fade in side by side without splitting it: a GREEN tag 'complementarity: species do better together' with cartoon deep and shallow roots and a legume nodule; a VIOLET tag 'selection: high-yielding species gain the most in mixture' with one oversized tuft whose bar grows most relative to its monoculture bar. A small '+' joins them: 'both can act at once'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Where could the extra come from? Perhaps the species use soil and light differently, or help each other. That is complementarity. Or a richer draw is more likely to include a species that yields highly alone. If such high-yielding species also gain the most relative to their yield alone, that is selection. Both can act at once.

scenes.tts: In a surveyed meadow, a wet patch can raise both species number and biomass. To separate richness from soil cleanly, ecologists sow richness at random.
scenes.visual: A wild meadow with a blue wet patch: arrows from 'wet soil' point to both 'more species' and 'more biomass', labelled 'confounder'. A hand then places seed packets on a grid of plots, with a die rolling beside it: 'richness assigned at random'. Schematic.
scenes.narration: In a surveyed meadow, a wet patch can raise both species number and biomass. To separate richness from soil cleanly, ecologists sow richness at random.

scenes.tts: Now let the years pass. Grown alone, one species bounces up and down from year to year. For its size, its total swings a lot.
scenes.visual: A year counter ticks 1 to 10. A single GOLD bar bounces up and down; a thin band beside it marks its typical swing. On-screen: 'mean 50, typical swing 25'. Computed from independent random draws.
scenes.narration: Now let the years pass. Grown alone, one species bounces up and down from year to year. For its size, its total swings a lot.

scenes.tts: Stack four species, each swinging by that same amount, independently of the others. Their swings do not depend on each other. The dark outline traces their total.
scenes.visual: Four bars, GOLD, TEAL, CORAL, SLATE BLUE, each bouncing out of step with the others, stacked; the DARK OUTLINE around the stack bounces too. On-screen per species: 'mean 50, swing 25'. Computed.
scenes.narration: Stack four species, each swinging by that same amount, independently of the others. Their swings do not depend on each other. The dark outline traces their total.

scenes.tts: Here is the question. Each species swings by the same amount. Will the total swing four times as much as a single species does?
scenes.visual: The stack freezes. Two option tags float beside the outline: 'swing x4' and 'less than x4'.
scenes.narration: Here is the question. Each species swings by the same amount. Will the total swing four times as much as a single species does?

scenes.visual: Hold the frame; a 5-second countdown; caption 'Predict: how much does the total swing?'

scenes.tts: No. The total swings only about twice as much, while its mean is four times larger. Good and bad years partly cancel in the sum. This is statistical averaging.
scenes.visual: Animation resumes. Beside the stack, on-screen: 'mean: 50 to 200 (x4)', 'swing: 25 to 50 (x2)', 'mean / swing: 2 to 4'. In two highlighted years, a CORAL bar dips while a TEAL bar rises, and the outline barely moves; label 'swings partly cancel'. Computed.
scenes.narration: No. The total swings only about twice as much, while its mean is four times larger. Good and bad years partly cancel in the sum. This is statistical averaging.

scenes.tts: But cancelling needs the species to swing out of step. If all four rose and fell together, nothing would cancel. The total would be no steadier than one species.
scenes.visual: The four bars now bounce in lockstep; the DARK OUTLINE swings hard. On-screen: 'all in step: mean x4, swing x4, mean / swing stays 2'. Label 'no cancelling'. Computed.
scenes.narration: But cancelling needs the species to swing out of step. If all four rose and fell together, nothing would cancel. The total would be no steadier than one species.

scenes.tts: So a field is a sum. Its extra is judged against what its monocultures predict. When species swing out of step, their swings partly cancel, and that can steady the sum.
scenes.visual: Recap strip of three small panels: the stacked mixture bar above the dashed expected bar with a GREEN and VIOLET '?' over the gap; the out-of-step stack with a calm outline; the lockstep stack with a wild outline crossed out. Caption 'judged against expected / swings partly cancel / not in lockstep'.
scenes.narration: So a field is a sum. Its extra is judged against what its monocultures predict. When species swing out of step, their swings partly cancel, and that can steady the sum.

scenes.visual: End card, one line only: 'A field is a sum, judged against expected; out-of-step swings partly cancel.'
